title: Devcase fakes answer in text: shape pin measured, a one-key tail can't win

gates.gate_note: tsc/typecheck/unit/perf non-zero exits are foreign-only (see notes); this card touches no TS

deviations_from_card: Re-sized to L per the critic; test_llm_expected_keys.py added to the write set and its provenance waiver deleted (table now empty, docstring updated). Counts corrected: 18 fakes lacked expected_keys (15 in-context + test_interview_scenario:46, test_match_reasoning:58,87) - measured by the same AST scan the new contract test runs. test_json_values.py needed no edit (its one-key tie cases stay green unchanged); the tie/coverage cases live in test_devcase_shape_pinning.SelectorRanksByCoverageTest. Matrix is stronger than the card: every expected key of each of the 10 steps gets its own one-key tail (44 key-rows) and a row holds only if there is no sentinel, the source is still llm AND the artifact equals the one the genuine answer alone produces - the last clause was needed because under the old selector assess_tooling (0/4) and score_transfer (1/4) tails that coerced away silently replaced the genuine answer with template values under 'llm' without leaking the sentinel. Non-vacuity measured: the pre-change selector turns 10 of 10 rows red (44/44 key-rows); the test asserts >=8 (card floor) and == all 10. Commit series: test (shared text fake + 18 migrated fakes, green on the pre-change selector: 145 tests in the 9 touched modules) / feat (selector + sniff retirement + waiver + matrix) / docs (under lock) - the feat commit carries the red-first acceptance file because it cannot be green without the code. notes: Red first on base (selector + provenance at a24bbe0f3): 7 of 15 test methods red, i.e. acceptance cases 1-5 red; case 6 (non-vacuity control) is green by construction. Behaviour change the ranking introduces (named per critic, pinned by test_the_named_behaviour_change_an_earlier_fuller_object_now_wins and stated in json_values docstring, llm-provider-layer.md and the dev-case README): an EARLIER parseable object covering strictly more expected keys than a genuine last answer that omits an optional key now wins. Optional-key-echo exposure: multi-key callers whose genuine answer may legitimately omit a key - jobseeker.py:1422 (accepts a missing 'artifact'), and in principle every multi-key pin (automation _generate x6, agentfit, jobseeker :1453/:1595, intake :1701, repo_scan, profile_draft, market_salary, group_compare, match_reasoning, the 10 devcase steps) - are exposed only if the model emits a PARSEABLE echo carrying more keys before its answer; pseudo-JSON example schemas do not parse, fenced answers still win, same-key echoes tie (last wins). Re-verified on today's tree: npm run test:python:gate green, 3061 tests, 0 failures, skipped 4 (KP_SKIP_BASELINE untouched) - the ranking breaks 0 existing tests.
